title: Senator Ted Stevens' Foo Fighter encounters
summary: Lou Elizondo tells of Senator Ted Stevens' Foo Fighter encounters, about World War II at wartime Europe, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

as_told.title: Senator Ted Stevens' World War II UFO sighting

plain: Ted Stevens flew as a pilot in World War II and later became a US senator for Alaska. Lue Elizondo, who says he ran a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, says Stevens helped found that office and admitted to running into "foo fighters" during the war, the name pilots gave to strange balls of light that followed their planes. A guest named Merrick also says Stevens saw a foo fighter, and ties him to Senator Harry Reid of Nevada, with whom he backed government UFO research. People tell it because it would mean one of the program's founders had seen something himself.
